title: Avinguda Meridiana · Fabra i Puig
description: The street outside the flat, rebuilt from OpenStreetMap, the city's design for the 2025-26 works and openly licensed photos: six lanes (two and a bus lane each way) with the planted median and its two-way bike lane, the 10 m panot sidewalk with the old plane trees in pits, granite kerbs lowered at the zebras, new black asphalt, blocks with balcony slabs, cornices, bare party walls and crowded terraces (stair housings, water tanks, aerials, air conditioners), Hipercor's vaulted canopy under the brown-banded slab, recycling containers, the Bicing dock, scooters and café tables; then the Fabra i Puig stair, which opens the network plan; the avenue from above; after rain (wet asphalt and puddles) and at dusk (shop light on the sidewalk).

steps.caption: Out of the portal at Meridiana 335: VivaGym on Gerard's right, the canopy with 335, Bluespace's ramp on his left, the gym's window running on into the next block
The even side: Granier, 365, Vision-Prix on the wide panot sidewalk, benches facing the shops, the kerb bed and the bus shelter
The median: the two-way bike lane between planted beds, young trees on stakes, the works' barriers and sacks, the vent grates over the trains (they breathe a pale draught when one runs underneath)
Hipercor from its own pavement, its back to the camera: the vaulted white canopy over the doors, seen through the box's window, and the graffiti hoarding
The L1's Concepció Arenal entrance to Fabra i Puig, on the even pavement by the Escòcia crossing: the totem with the M, L1 and the name, the stair going down between granite and glass
Walking into the stair opens the network plan on the station wall, framed on Fabra i Puig and Trinitat Vella, the trip dashed with its stops
− (or the wheel) zooms out to the whole city; dragging pans, + zooms in
Esc goes back up: Gerard stands at the entrance again
The avenue from above, from home (left) to the Fabra i Puig crossing (right), Hipercor nearest the camera: six lanes and the median, the blocks' terraces, the city going on in the haze
Café Entrepans' tables on the wide sidewalk, a bench and a lamp by the kerb bed, the old plane trees in their pits and the kiosk on the corner
Rain: the asphalt and the panot darken and shine, puddles gather in the gutters along the kerbs
Nine in the evening: the open shops spill warm light on the sidewalk, the LED lamps a cold one (her pink creeps in with the dusk)
